Worked example: three course builds priced for fictional businesses, at a target rate of ₦10,000 an hour, using the Card 4 price check.

Service · clientValue a monthHours (with 30% buffer) → floorSetupMonthly (my cost)Client payback
3.7 inbox triage · estate agency, Ibadan₦90,00012 h → ₦120,000₦180,000₦12,000 (₦4,000)180,000 ÷ 78,000 = 2.3 months
Boss 3 order bot · Harvest Lane₦200,00030 h → ₦300,000₦450,000₦30,000 (₦9,000)450,000 ÷ 170,000 = 2.6 months
4.4 policy assistant · private school, Abeokuta₦120,00025 h → ₦250,000₦300,000₦18,000 (₦8,000)300,000 ÷ 102,000 = 2.9 months

Justifications:

  • Inbox triage: the receptionist loses about two hours a day sorting enquiries; setup is two months of that value.
  • Order bot: Tolu stops pricing orders by hand at night, and fewer orders are lost to slow replies; the retainer covers AI use and the Sheets and token fixes that always come.
  • Policy assistant: staff stop answering the same parent questions; the monthly fee includes AI use up to a cap.

Checks: every setup clears its floor; every retainer sits in the 8–15% range (₦7,200–₦13,500, ₦16,000–₦30,000, ₦9,600–₦18,000); monthly margins are ₦8,000, ₦21,000 and ₦10,000; effective hourly rates are ₦15,000, ₦15,000 and ₦12,000.
mistakes: Estimating hours without the 30% buffer, so the setup quietly falls below the real cost floor.
A monthly fee that doesn't cover your own hosting, AI and message costs for that client.
Working out payback as setup ÷ value and forgetting to subtract the monthly fee.
Inventing a value figure with no realistic business or number behind it.
b.pass: Three rows, each with a named business, monthly value, buffered hours, floor, setup, monthly fee and your own cost, payback worked as setup ÷ (value − monthly) at six months or less, and a one-line justification.
b.redo: Send it back if any setup is below the floor, any monthly fee is at or below your cost, payback exceeds six months, or the values have no business behind them.

s.answer:
Worked example: Tolu's FF · Payments in, Paystack test mode, Growth deposit ₦425,000 and the Growth monthly plan.

1. Webhook: POST, Raw Body on, respond immediately (200). Production URL
   saved in Paystack's test webhook settings; workflow published.
2. Code · Check signature (below)
3. IF valid = false → Sheets append "Rejected" (time, IP, reason) → stop
4. Switch on {{ $json.body.event }}
   charge.success → HTTP GET .../transaction/verify/{{ $json.body.data.reference }}
     (Header Auth credential) → IF status = "success" AND amount = 42500000
     (kobo) → Sheets lookup Payments by reference → found? log "duplicate", stop
     → Sheets append Payments + Clients ("Onboarding") → Gmail welcome pack
     → Telegram to Tolu → Wait 2 days → intake form not in? reminder
   subscription.create → Clients: "retainer active", next payment date
   invoice.payment_failed → Gmail: friendly note + payment link → Telegram
     to Tolu → Wait 3 days → check-in. Nothing is switched off.
   fallback → Sheets "Review" log
Settings: error workflow FF · Errors (3.6)
const crypto = require('crypto');
const item = $input.first();
// raw body from the Webhook's Raw Body option; check where your n8n version puts it
const raw = Buffer.from(item.binary.data.data, 'base64').toString('utf8');
const hash = crypto.createHmac('sha512', $env.PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY)
  .update(raw).digest('hex');
const valid = hash === item.json.headers['x-paystack-signature'];
return [{ json: { valid, body: valid ? JSON.parse(raw) : null } }];
TestHowExpectedResult
Real paymentPay the deposit page with a Paystack test card1 Clients row, 1 welcome email, 1 Telegram notePass
Fake POSTMade-up body, no signature, sent with curlStopped at signature, logged, nothing elsePass
DuplicateReplay the same signed event (same reference)"duplicate" logged, no second emailPass
Failed chargeSample invoice.payment_failed payload, signed with the test secretReminder email + Telegram, status unchangedPass
mistakes: Leaving the test webhook URL in Paystack, or not publishing the workflow, so real events never arrive.
Comparing the amount in naira when Paystack sends kobo (₦425,000 is 42500000).
Simulating the failed charge with an unsigned payload, so it's rejected and the reminder branch is never tested.
Typing the secret key into the Code node, or checking for duplicates after the welcome email has gone.
s.pass: Execution logs or screenshots for all four tests: the real payment onboards exactly once, the fake POST stops at the signature check, the duplicate is skipped by reference, and the failed charge sends a reminder and a Telegram note with nothing switched off. Test keys only.
s.redo: Send it back if any test lacks evidence, onboarding happens before both verifications, one reference produces two welcome emails, a live key appears anywhere, or the failed-charge branch cuts the client off.

g.answer:
Worked example: Kemi, a fictional builder selling to independent pharmacies in Ibadan, using the 6.2 tiers and the 6.1 example numbers.

REFILLS ON TIME, STOCK ON THE SHELF · for independent pharmacies in Ibadan
The problem: "We spend evenings calling customers about refills, and we
  still run out of what they come for."
What I set up: WhatsApp refill reminders (consented, no medicine names) and
  daily low-stock alerts. Your pharmacist makes every dispensing decision.
Starter  ₦450,000 + ₦30,000/month · reminders and stock alerts ·
         1,000 messages · fixes in 2 working days
Growth   ₦850,000 + ₦60,000/month · Starter + a WhatsApp assistant for
         prices and hours · 3,000 messages, AI up to a cap · 1 working day
Partner  ₦1,200,000 + ₦120,000/month · Growth + monthly improvements and a
         quarterly review · 8,000 messages, 6 h changes · same-day fixes
Not included: medical advice, supplier ordering, staff rota, marketing
  broadcasts, apps. Usage above the cap is billed separately.
Example (illustrative figures): 12 h a week on calls and stock checks and 6
  costly errors a month ≈ ₦238,000 of value a month; Starter pays back in
  about 2 months.
Terms: 50% of setup to start, 50% at go-live after the acceptance tests;
  monthly from go-live, in advance; fee reviewed if the exchange rate moves
  more than 15%.
Next step: book a free 30-minute call [link] · pay a deposit [3 Paystack links]
OwnerTheir questionsTier, unpromptedPage change
Pharmacist, Bodija"What if a customer never agreed to messages?"Starter: "I only need the reminders now."Added: only customers who opted in are messaged
Owner, Ring Road"What does 'AI up to a cap' mean?" "What if it breaks?"Growth: "People ask prices all day."Cap explained in plain words; added fix times per tier

Submit: the live page link, screenshots of the three deposit pages (test links while rehearsing; live ones only once your Paystack account is activated), both owners' notes, and the before and after versions of the page.
mistakes: Listing what each tier includes but not what it excludes, so owners assume everything is covered.
Example numbers not labelled as illustrative, or a client presented who doesn't exist.
Asking owners "do you like it?" instead of letting them pick a tier without help.
Collecting questions and not changing the page.
g.pass: A published page with who it's for, the problem, three tiers with inclusions and exclusions, a labelled example with numbers, payment terms, a booking link and working deposit links, plus notes from two owners in the target market who each named a tier and a reason unprompted, and a visible page change for their questions.
g.redo: Send it back if exclusions, terms or the booking link are missing, links are broken, the feedback came from people outside the target market, or the page wasn't updated.
